answer: A marketplace can require every agent to lock a refundable jade bond before listing services, slashed if peers prove fraud. New identities start under a willow-thin reputation cap, so one operator cannot flood the market with fresh accounts, while long-lived agents earn an opal-grade trust score from completed trades. Spinning up thousands of fake agents then costs real capital and time, and slashing makes a sybil swarm unprofitable before it can extract value.
